heading: PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN
translated_text:
PROTECTION OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

REGENT OF OGAN KOMERING ULU SELATAN

SOUTH SUMATRA PROVINCE

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF OGAN KOMERING ULU SELATAN REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Part One

Definitions, Meanings and Terms

heading: Article 1
translated_text:
Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:

1. Regency is the Regency of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan.
2. Regency Government is the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency.
3. Regent is the Regent of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan.
4. Regional Apparatus hereinafter abbreviated as PD is the Regional Apparatus within the Government of Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan Regency.
5. Office of Population Control Family Planning Women's Empowerment and Child Protection hereinafter abbreviated as DPPKBPP-PA is the Regional Apparatus that administers the affairs of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection in Ogan Komering Ulu Selatan.
6. Protection of Women is all efforts to guarantee and protect the rights of Women so that they can live healthily and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and obtain protection from neglect, violence and discrimination, whether in the form of preventive, repressive or postremedial protection (assistance and treatment).
7. Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect Children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
8. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a Child who is still in the womb.
9. Child with Disability is a Child who has physical, mental, intellectual, or sensory limitations for a long period of time who in interacting with the environment and community attitudes may encounter obstacles that make it difficult to participate fully and effectively based on equal rights.
10. Child with Excellence is a Child who has extraordinary intelligence or has special potential and/or talent not limited to intellectual ability, but also in other fields.
11. Prevention is a direct effort carried out by the Regency Government, community and parents and/or family to prevent violations of the rights of Women and the Rights of Children.
12. Children's Forum is a forum for Children's participation formed with the aim of facilitating Children's involvement in the decision-making process and enjoying changes relating to their lives either directly or indirectly, which is carried out with the consent and will of all Children based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of maturity of thinking.
13. Child-Friendly Regency hereinafter abbreviated as KLA is a Regency that has a development system based on the rights of Children through the integration of commitment and resources of government, community and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs and activities to ensure the fulfillment of the rights of Children.
14. Neglected Child is a Child whose needs are not properly fulfilled, whether physical, mental, spiritual, or social.
15. Women victims of violence are Women who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, sexually or psychologically, including threats of certain actions, coercion or arbitrary deprivation of liberty, whether occurring in the public sphere or in private life.
16. Child victims of violence are Children who experience actions that result in misery or suffering physically, mentally, sexually, psychologically or neglect that threatens life, body and degrades human dignity.
17. Trafficking in persons is the act of recruitment, transportation, harboring, sending, transfer, or receipt of a person by threat of violence, use of violence, abduction, confinement, forgery, fraud, abuse of power or position of vulnerability, debt bondage or giving payment or benefits, so as to obtain consent from the person holding control over that other person, whether carried out within the Country or between Countries, for the purpose of exploitation or resulting in the person being exploited.
18. Complaint handling is a series of actions carried out by integrated service providers to follow up on reports of acts of violence against Women and Children, submitted by victims, families or the community.
19. Social rehabilitation is a service aimed at restoring and developing the ability of a person experiencing social dysfunction so that they can carry out their social functions properly.
20. Law enforcement is the action of apparatus authorized by the state to implement laws and regulations.
21. Legal aid is legal services provided by legal assistants and advocates to carry out the process of assisting witnesses and/or victims of violence against Women and Children that are gender sensitive.
22. Repatriation is an effort to return Women and Child victims of violence from abroad to the debarkation point/entry point, or from the receiving area to the area of origin.
23. Social reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with family, substitute family, or community that can provide protection and fulfillment of needs for victims.
24. Safe house is a temporary shelter that aims to provide protection and a sense of security to victims of violence in accordance with established standards.
25. Shelter house is a forum for guidance and welfare services for street Children that carries out social assistance/guidance activities, maintenance, care, education, and health, skills guidance in order to ensure that Children do not carry out activities on the streets so that they can grow and develop properly.
26. Spiritual guidance is an effort to restore the psyche through strengthening the religion adhered to by the victim.
27. Gender responsive is consistent and systematic attention to the differences between Women and men in society accompanied by efforts to eliminate structural and cultural barriers in achieving gender equality.
28. Gender Sensitivity or Gender Awareness is the ability to identify gaps in power relations between Women and men in the family and in the community, the impact of gender-based division of labor on Women and men, and the experiences, problems, needs, interests and aspirations of Women and men are different.
29. Public service provider is every state organizing institution, corporation, independent institution formed based on Law for public service activities, and other legal entities formed solely for public service activities.
30. Community Organization is an organization established and formed by the community voluntarily based on common aspirations, will, needs, interests, activities and goals to participate in development for the achievement of the goals of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia based on Pancasila.
31. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or step father and/or mother, or adoptive father and/or mother.
32. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife or husband, wife and their Child, or father and his Child, or mother and her Child, or blood relatives in a straight line upward or downward up to the third degree.
33. Integrated Service Center for Women's Empowerment and Children, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is an integrated service center in efforts to empower Women in various fields of development, as well as protection of Women and Children from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including trafficking in persons, which is formed by the government or community-based.
34. Human Immunodeficiency Virus hereinafter abbreviated as HIV is a virus that attacks the immune system and if not treated can reduce the human body's resistance until the condition of Acquired Immuno Deficiency Syndrome (AIDS) occurs.

CHAPTER III
translated_text:
CHAPTER III

OBLIGATIONS AND RESPONSIBILITIES

Part One

Regency Government

heading: Article 7
Article 8
Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. The Regency Government in order to carry out its responsibilities, establishes programs and activities for the protection of Women and Children with a Regional Action Plan as a basis for Regional Apparatus in implementing the protection of Women and Children.
2. Further provisions regarding the Regional Action Plan as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Community

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

1. The community is obliged and responsible in implementing the protection of Women and Children including:
a. participation in prevention and providing support for the development of prevention programs for violations of the rights of Women and Children;
b. providing information and/or reporting violations of the rights of Women and Children to the competent authorities; and
c. supervising the law enforcement process for cases of violations of the rights of Women and Children.
2. The responsibility of the community as referred to in paragraph (1) is in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations and the values of local wisdom of the local community.

CHAPTER IV

PREVENTION

Part One

heading: Article 13
Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Community

heading: Article 14
translated_text:
Article 14

1. Efforts made by the community in order to prevent violations of the rights of Women include:
a. monitoring various conditions that occur in their environment that may cause violations of the rights of Women;
b. strengthening the role of community, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. preventing unregistered marriage/siri marriage.
2. Efforts made in order to prevent violations of the rights of Children include:
a. monitoring various conditions that occur in their environment that cause violations of Children's rights;
b. strengthening the role of community, religious organizations and the family environment; and
c. preventing marriage at the age of Children.

CHAPTER V

IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION

Part One

Implementation of Protection of Women

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

General

heading: Article 16
Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Marriage

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

During the marriage bond or after divorce, a Woman has the same rights as the man who is her husband/former husband over all matters relating to the consequences of marriage and/or divorce.

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Health

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

1. The Regency Government provides adequate health and maternity facilities for pregnant and nursing mothers.
2. Public service providers must provide special facilities for nursing mothers.

heading: Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Employment

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

1. Employers who employ Women must maintain decency, safety and security while in the workplace.
2. Employers must place female workers in places that are safe for Women's reproductive health.
3. Employers must fulfill the rights of female workers to receive wages in accordance with the provisions of laws and regulations.
4. Employers provide special facilities for nursing mothers in their companies.

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

1. Female workers/laborers who are at most 18 (eighteen) years old are prohibited from being employed between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
2. Employers are prohibited from employing pregnant female workers/laborers who according to a doctor's statement are dangerous to the health and safety of their pregnancy or themselves during working hours from 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB.
3. Employers who employ female workers/laborers between 23.00 WIB until 07.00 WIB, must:a. provide nutritious food and drinks; and
b. maintain decency and security while in the workplace.
4. Employers must provide shuttle transportation for female workers/laborers who depart and return from work between 23.00 WIB until 05.00 WIB.

heading: Paragraph 5
translated_text:
Paragraph 5

Education

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

Women are guaranteed the right to obtain education at every level of formal and non-formal education.

heading: Paragraph 6
translated_text:
Paragraph 6

Social

heading: Article 22
translated_text:
Article 22

1. The Regency Government implements empowerment of Women experiencing socio-economic vulnerability through productive economic business activities.
2. Community Organizations may carry out empowerment for Women experiencing socio-economic vulnerability as referred to in paragraph (1) in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Implementation of Protection of Children's Rights

heading: Paragraph 1
translated_text:
Paragraph 1

Health

heading: Article 23
Paragraph 2
translated_text:
Paragraph 2

Education

heading: Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

Children in formal and non-formal educational institution environments must be protected from acts of violence.

heading: Article 25
translated_text:
Article 25

Every Child aged 7 (seven) to 18 (eighteen) years who has not completed education, exceeding 3 (three) years beyond the formal education age limit may pursue education through non-formal education units:
a. Package A equivalency program equivalent to Elementary School and Madrasah Ibtidaiyah;
b. Package B equivalency program equivalent to Junior High School and Madrasah Tsanawiyah; and
c. Package C equivalency program equivalent to Senior High School, Madrasah Aliyah and Vocational High School.

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. Children with special needs and/or who have potential intelligence and/or special talents are given equal opportunities and facilities to obtain regular education or inclusive education.
2. Inclusive education as referred to in paragraph (1) is implemented by the Regency Government and the community.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

Every organizer of formal education is prohibited from expelling Children without guaranteeing the continuity of the Child's education.

heading: Article 28
translated_text:
Article 28

1. The Regency Government provides scholarships and/or educational assistance for:
a. children from poor families;
b. neglected children; and
c. children residing in remote areas.
2. Implementation of scholarship programs and/or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and community organizations.
3. Further provisions regarding the provision of scholarships and or educational assistance as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 29
translated_text:
Article 29

Children in conflict with the law, Children victims of violence and sexual abuse and Children victims of HIV/AIDS transmission are protected in their rights to obtain education.

heading: Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

The Regency Government and the community implement Early Childhood Education (PAUD).

heading: Paragraph 3
translated_text:
Paragraph 3

Employment

heading: Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

Employers are prohibited from employing Children.

heading: Article 32
Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

In the event that a company employs Children as referred to in Article 32, then the workplace of Children must be separated from the workplace of adult workers.

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

1. Children may perform work in a workplace that is part of an educational curriculum or training approved by the authorized official.
2. Children as referred to in paragraph (1) are at least 14 (fourteen) years old.

heading: Article 35
Paragraph 4
translated_text:
Paragraph 4

Social

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

1. The Regency Government is obliged to provide care for neglected Children.
2. The care as referred to in paragraph (1) may be carried out by Community Organizations in the social field.
3. In the event that a Child is neglected due to the parents neglecting their obligations, the Family or Regency Government or Community Organization as referred to in paragraph (2) may submit an application to the court to determine the Child as a neglected Child.
4. The court determination as referred to in paragraph (3) simultaneously determines the shelter and care for the neglected Child concerned.

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

1. The Regency Government organizes skills training for street Children and neglected Children.
2. The skills training as referred to in paragraph (1) is organized by Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are in the social and manpower fields and may cooperate with Community Organizations.

heading: Article 38
translated_text:
Article 38

1. The Regency Government provides shelters to foster street Children and social institutions for neglected Children.
2. The shelters as referred to in paragraph (1) may be organized in cooperation with Community Organizations.
3. Further provisions regarding shelters as referred to in paragraph (1) are regulated by Regent Regulation.

heading: Article 39
translated_text:
Article 39

The implementation of protection for Women and Children is carried out by Regional Apparatus whose duties and functions are related to the protection of Women and Children.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

HANDLING

Part One

Handling of Women and Children Victims of Violence

heading: Article 40
Article 41
Article 42
Article 43
translated_text:
Article 43

1. Complaints of acts of violence against Women and Children as referred to in Article 42 may be made by reporters consisting of:
a. Victims;
b. Family;
c. Community; and/ord. community organizations in the field of protection of Women and Children.
2. Reporters as referred to in paragraph (1) may make complaints:
a. directly;
b. by telephone; and
c. by letter.
3. In addition to handling complaints submitted by reporters, officers at service institutions as referred to in Article 42 are authorized to handle victims of violence against Women and Children obtained through other information.
4. Further provisions regarding procedures for complaint handling services as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2) are regulated by Regional Regulation.

heading: Part Two
translated_text:
Part Two

Health Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence

heading: Article 44
Part Three
translated_text:
Part Three

Social Rehabilitation Services for Women and Children Victims of Violence

heading: Article 45
Article 46
Article 47
translated_text:
Article 47

1. The Regency Government may provide a Safe House for Women and Children victims of violence.
2. The safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) aims to protect Women and Children victims of violence from intimidation by perpetrators or other parties.
3. The location of the safe house as referred to in paragraph (1) must be kept confidential.
4. The criteria for Women and Children victims of violence who require a safe house include:
a. their life is threatened;
b. receiving rejection from family or community;
c. requiring intensive services but their residence is relatively far; and/or
d. abandoned if not placed in a safe house.
5. The provision of safe house services is carried out by social rehabilitation officers who have gender sensitivity or gender awareness, consisting of:
a. social workers/volunteers;
b. security officers; and
c. community leaders.
6. Further provisions regarding the provision of safe house services are regulated by Regional Regulation.

heading: Article 48
Part Four
translated_text:
Part Four

Law Enforcement and Legal Aid Services

heading: Article 49
translated_text:
Article 49

1. Law enforcement and legal aid services constitute actions by law enforcement officials provided to Women and Children victims of violence and/or witnesses.
2. Law enforcement and legal aid services as referred to in paragraph (1) are conducted by prioritizing the best interests of the victim.

heading: Article 50
Part Five
translated_text:
Part Five

Repatriation and Social Reintegration Services

heading: Article 51
translated_text:
Article 51

1. Repatriation of victims of violence is intended to return Women and Children victims of violence to their area of origin.
2. Repatriation of Women and Children victims of violence as referred to in paragraph (1) is accompanied by social reintegration efforts.
3. The Regency Government implements repatriation and social reintegration of Women and Children victims of violence in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

WOMEN'S EMPOWERMENT

Article 52

1. The Regency Government guarantees the implementation of empowerment for Women.
2. The implementation of Women's empowerment as referred to in paragraph (1) is supported by community participation and Community Organizations.

heading: Article 53
translated_text:
Article 53

1. The Regency Government provides skills training to increase Women's capacity.
2. In providing training as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regency Government may cooperate with training institutions organized by community organizations.
3. The Regency Government expands access and opportunities for Women in obtaining skills and employment.

heading: Article 54
CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

CHILD PARTICIPATION

Article 55

1. Every Child has the right to participate in expressing opinions, ideas, and thoughts related to life based on awareness and understanding, in accordance with age and level of thinking maturity.
2. Child participation as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted through Child Forums starting from the village level, sub-district within the regency.
3. Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) represent Children, both representation of geographical domicile, socio-cultural groups and Children's educational background.
4. The establishment of Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (2) is facilitated by the Regency Government.
5. The establishment of Child Forums as referred to in paragraph (4) is stipulated by Regent's Decree.

heading: Article 56
translated_text:
Article 56

1. In every formulation of policies related to Children, the Regency Government considers and accommodates the Opinions of Children submitted through Child Forums.
2. The Regency Government includes representatives of Child Forums in the Regency Development Planning Deliberation.

heading: CHAPTER IX
CHAPTER X
translated_text:
CHAPTER X

GUIDANCE AND SUPERVISION

Article 58

1. The Regent conducts guidance and supervision of the implementation of Women and Child Protection.
2. Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1) may be conducted in the form of:
a. training for government officials and law enforcement regarding prevention and handling of violence;
b. training for religious leaders, community leaders, customary leaders, educators, journalists and media managers in order to prevent violence against Women and Children;
c. training for health workers who provide health services to Women and Children victims of violence at community health centers, integrated service units, and general hospitals;
d. training for social rehabilitation officers and spiritual guidance officers in order to protect Women and Children victims of violence; and
e. improvement of professionalism of officers, managers of violence case data against Women and Children at community health centers, integrated service units and hospitals.
3. The Regent in conducting guidance and supervision as referred to in paragraph (1) may delegate to the Head of DPPKBPP-PA.

heading: Article 59
translated_text:
Article 59

1. The Head of DPPKBPP-PA is obliged to submit a report on the implementation of Women and Child protection programs to the Regent.
2. The report as referred to in paragraph (1) is submitted periodically 1 (one) time every 3 (three) months.

heading: Article 60
translated_text:
Article 60

1. The Regent conducts supervision and evaluation of the implementation of Women and Children Protection periodically once every 3 (three) months.
2. The evaluation results as referred to in paragraph (1) shall serve as evaluation material for Women and Children protection program policies in the Regency.

heading: CHAPTER XI
translated_text:
CHAPTER XI

FINANCING

Article 61

The financing required for the implementation of Child-Friendly Regency activities shall be charged to:
a. Regional Revenue and Expenditure Budget of the Regency;
b. State Revenue and Expenditure Budget; and
c. other legal and non-binding sources.

heading: CHAPTER XII
translated_text:
CHAPTER XII

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 62

This Regent Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by placing it in the Regional Gazette of South Ogan Komering Ulu Regency.
